episodes.177063: An upper trough moved eastward across central California on March 4 and March 5. This system produced snow at elevations down to 2000 feet with some higher elevation  SNOTELS north of Kings Canyon picking up between a foot and 2 feet of new snowfall. Thunderstorms broke out in the San Joaquin Valley during the afternoon and evening of March 5 producing widespread nuisance flooding and small hail. In addition, outflow gusts from some of the thunderstorms downed some trees.
episodes.177140: One to two inches of rain fell across the Upper Wabash River basin on March 3rd, causing the Wabash River to rise well into minor flood stage on the 5th and 6th of March. A driver disregarded road closed signs in rural Adams county near the Wabash River and subsequently drown after driving into the high water.
episodes.178364: Most of the Ohio, Wabash, Little Wabash, and Big Muddy Rivers rose above flood stage early in the month. The flooding was all minor, consisting mostly of fields and woodlands in the low bottomlands. Some flood-prone secondary roads along the rivers were flooded. March came in like a lion, with a large and intense storm system early in the month. Daily rounds of showers and storms with moderate to heavy rainfall occurred across the region. Rainfall totals were between 3 and 4.5 inches.
episodes.179418: Several weak waterspouts were observed in association with a convective cloud line along the oceanside of the Lower Florida Keys.  Light northeast lower tropospheric flow was present.

events.narrative: California Highway Patrol reported a tree on all lanes of Rd. 96.
An NWS employee noticed storm damage from a blown down tree next to his house where several tree branches were on the street and had destroyed a car.

Indiana DNR officials reported a 55 year old male was driving north on County Road 300 West, north of County Road 850 South and disregarded road closed signs due to high water levels on the Wabash River. The driver's van entered the flood water at approximately 430 am EST and began to submerge. He left the van in an effort to exit the flood waters, but was subsequently found deceased roughly 50 yards southwest of the submerged van by first responders.

events.narrative: Four nearly-stationary waterspouts were observed southwest of Cudjoe Key.  The condensation funnel clouds were narrow with only one extending as far as halfway from cloud base to the water surface.  No spray rings were observed.  The average duration was 8 minutes for the first three waterspouts, with the last waterspout ongoing as of the end report time of 9:41 am EST.
